Territorial Acknowledgment

Thompson Rivers University campuses are on the ancestral lands of the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc (Kamloops campus) and the T’exelc (Williams Lake campus) within Secwepemcúl̓ecw, the traditional and unceded territory of the Secwépemc. The region TRU serves also extends into the territories of the St’át’imc, Nlaka’pamux, Nuxalk, Tŝilhqot'in, Dakelh, and Syilx peoples.

slides.title: Study Tips
slides.body:
Study Tips

We are using a streamlined version of the textbook, so all textbook contents, as well as all lecture content, is material that you need to know for the exam
Please read the textbook to help clarify difficult materials (before and/or after lecture)
Please take notes during the lecture
Actively study the material after each lecture (not just re-reading/re-writing):
compare and contrast cells, organs, tissues, etc.
flowchart processes
draw figures
connect information across sections
Test yourself on the information the next day:
pretend that you are the teacher and teach the materials to an imaginary audience
do so on a paper or whiteboard with your study materials put away
figure out where you got stuck or made errors, and focus more study time on those areas of need
Once you have learned the information, then studying in a group can be useful:
teach each other the information
if you do not all agree on something, then perhaps one of you learned it wrong – double check the info
Come to office hours for help; bring prepared questions
Do not be tempted into using generative AI to complete unproctored assignments, as you will not develop the study and test-taking skills needed to succeed during proctored examinations.
